newsitem.title: USA: Lawsuit against Clinton dismissed, with a warning.
newsitem.headline: Lawsuit against Clinton dismissed, with a warning.

text.p: A federal judge dismissed Thursday a lawsuit by 41 House members against President Clinton on missile defence, but warned he would not allow the White House to defy Congress indefinitely.

U.S. District Judge Stanley Sporkin's ruling ended a House attempt to get legal help to stop the Clinton administration from ignoring a law passed by Congress on funding for anti-missiles to protect U.S. troops and allies as Patriot missiles did in the 1991 Gulf War.
The judge said his court should not yet get involved because Congress and the Clinton administration might resolve differences over the missile spending.
If not, he warned, "this court will revisit the critical issues presented here."
"This court will not condone the executive branch defying the explicit laws enacted by Congress," he said.

The legislators, including House National Security Committee Chairman Floyd Spence, a South Carolina Republican, accused Clinton of defying a law requiring that the administration give spending priority to two of the most sophisticated U.S. anti-missiles being developed.

They are the U.S. Army's Theatre High-Altitude Area Defence (THAAD) missile and the Navy's Upper Tier missile, which would shoot down enemy missiles much higher and further from allied troops and cities than the Patriots did.

Clinton's Defence Department instead decided to give priority spending to anti-missiles that would not destroy enemy missiles as high and far away but, it said, can be developed and put into operation faster.
